proposal.observation: detected_lines.png: 10 magenta vertical ring boundaries are regularly spaced (~245 px) across the full 2400 px width, consistent with ring_count_error=0. Oblique line yield is very low: only ~15 short green/red segments, all confined to the mid-band y~1420-1640 and to x<1600 (rings 1-7); rings 8-10 have no oblique lines at all, and one blue horizontal fallback segment appears at y~770. The outlier map shows the circumferential joints at y~770, ~1600 and ~2300 only as broken dotted traces, so Hough fragments never reach accumulator threshold and gaps are not bridged. initial_prompt_points.png confirms that all 10 prompt centres are 'propagated' at a single y~1520 rather than directly detected per ring. depth_map_viridis.png: NaN regions are a left-edge strip, three horizontal joint bands and a genuine bottom-right void (depth_nan_ratio 0.195), i.e. moderate holes, not the dominant issue. segmentation_results.png: K band is placed at the mid joint band and ring stripes are coherent, but sam_fill_rate is 0.57 and correspondence_f1@15 only 0.24 with chamfer 74.7 px, indicating per-ring block boundaries are offset from the real joints because prompt centres are inferred from a single propagated row instead of ring-specific intersections.
proposal.rule: d7 (stage_4_detection): m_line_yield low AND horizontal fallback triggered -> f_missing_lines. Upstream check per inter_stage_dependencies: joint traces are visible in the outlier map (m_joint_contrast moderate, not absent) and m_hole_ratio is moderate, so f_joint_oversmoothed / f_depth_holes are not the primary cause; remediation r_relax_hough applies (lower oblique threshold, raise maxLineGap). Downstream chain f_missing_lines -> unstable prompt centres -> f_crop_offset explains low correspondence_f1@15 and sub-par sam_fill_rate.
proposal.rationale: Ring count and vertical band are already correct, so hough_threshold_vertical, unfolding (despite being unlocked, the depth map is well unrolled and the worked examples show that unfolding+denoising changes jointly collapsed sam_fill_rate and inflated depth_nan_ratio), denoising and SAM geometry are left untouched to avoid perturbing the two measurements that are currently healthy. The overlay is confined to the detection stage where the observed deficiency lies: hough_threshold_oblique lowered to 30 and maxLineGap_oblique raised to 50 so the dotted joint traces are bridged into full oblique segments across all 10 rings; binary_threshold lowered modestly to 115 so weaker outlier pixels on the joint traces survive binarisation; pattern_tolerance raised to 12 so the K/AB distance-pattern check accepts directly detected intersections instead of falling back to a propagated row. Worked example s019 (oblique 49, maxLineGap 53, binary 118, tolerance 16) was the mildest of the three joint degradations and kept ring_count_error at 0, suggesting these detection-side values are tolerable; unlike s019 this overlay does not move unfolding, denoising or SAM, which were the shared ingredients of the fill-rate collapse. Expected response: higher oblique line yield, ring-specific prompt centres, improved correspondence_f1@15 and sam_fill_rate, with ring_count_error and depth_nan_ratio unchanged.
